p.src: Now when Baoyu heard what Sheyue said, he fell backward and once more seemed to die, leaving Lady Wang and the others weeping and calling out without cease. Sheyue knew that her careless words had brought about this calamity, but just then Lady Wang and the others had no time to reproach her. As Sheyue wept, she made up her mind, thinking, “If Baoyu dies, I shall take my own life and follow him!” But let us say no more of what was in Sheyue’s heart. Let us instead tell how Lady Wang and the others, seeing that Baoyu could not be called back, hurriedly sent someone out to find the monk and ask him to save Baoyu. But when Jia Zheng went back out after entering the inner rooms, the monk had already vanished. Jia Zheng was still wondering at this when he heard another commotion within and hastened back inside. He saw Baoyu again in his former state, his jaws clenched tight and no breath or pulse remaining. Yet when he placed a hand over Baoyu’s heart, the flesh was still warm. Jia Zheng could only summon a physician in haste and have medicine poured into Baoyu in an effort to revive him.

p.src: Little did they know that Baoyu’s soul had long since left his body. Do you suppose, then, that he was dead? In fact, he had wandered in a daze to the front hall, where he saw the monk who had brought back the jade sitting there, and bowed to him. The monk unexpectedly rose, took Baoyu by the hand, and led him away. Following the monk, Baoyu felt as light as a leaf, drifting and swaying along; without even passing through the main gate, he somehow found himself outside. After traveling for a while, they came to a desolate wilderness, where in the distance he saw a memorial arch that seemed familiar. Just as he was about to ask the monk about it, a woman appeared dimly through the haze. Baoyu thought, “How could such a beautiful woman appear in a wilderness like this? She must be an immortal descended to the mortal world.” With this thought, Baoyu drew near and looked carefully. She did seem familiar, but for the moment he could not recall who she was. The woman came face-to-face with the monk and immediately disappeared. On reflection, Baoyu realized that she looked exactly like Third Sister You, which left him more puzzled than ever. “What is she doing here too?” As he was again about to ask, the monk pulled him through the arch. On its tablet were written four large characters, “Blessed Land of True Suchness,” and on either side hung this couplet:

p.src: When falsehood departs and truth arrives, truth surpasses falsehood; what arose from nothing is being, yet being is not nothing.

p.src: After reading this, Baoyu thought, “So that is how it is. I should like to ask about the coming and going of cause and consequence.” As this thought crossed his mind, he saw Yuanyang standing there, beckoning to him. Baoyu thought, “I have been walking all this time, yet I never left the Garden. How has it changed its appearance?” He hurried over to speak with Yuanyang, but in the blink of an eye she vanished, and he could not help growing suspicious. When he reached the place where Yuanyang had been standing, he found a row of side halls, each bearing its own inscribed tablet. Baoyu had no interest in looking at them and ran straight toward the spot where Yuanyang had stood. The door of one side hall stood half open. Baoyu did not dare enter rashly and was just about to ask the monk when, turning around, he discovered that the monk had long since disappeared. Still dazed, Baoyu saw that the halls were lofty and magnificent, wholly unlike anything in Prospect Garden. He stopped and looked up at the tablet, which read: “Leading the Passion-Besotted to Awakening.” On either side was written this couplet:

p.src: Baoyu suddenly remembered: “I once came to this place in a dream when I was young. To be able to come here in person now is a great stroke of fortune.” In his daze, he forgot all about looking for Yuanyang. Plucking up his courage, he opened the uppermost cabinet and looked inside. Seeing several registers there, he was more delighted than ever and thought, “People generally say that dreams are unreal, but little do they know that wherever there is such a dream, there is such a reality. I often wished to dream this dream again, but could never do so; who would have thought that today I should find this place? I wonder whether that register is the one I saw before?” He reached up and took down a volume. On its cover was written: “Principal Register of the Twelve Beauties of Jinling.” Holding it, Baoyu thought, “I dimly remember that this was the one; how vexing that I cannot recall it clearly.” He opened it to the first page and saw a picture, but the lines were so blurred that he could no longer make it out. Several lines of writing below were also unclear, though he could still trace their general shape. Looking closely, he made out something about a “jade belt,” and above it a character resembling “Lin.” He thought, “Could this be referring to Cousin Lin?” He looked more intently and saw below the four characters “a golden hairpin in the snow.” Astonished, he said, “Why does that look like her name as well?” He then read the four lines together from beginning to end and said, “There is no particular sense to them; they merely conceal the names of those two, which is nothing remarkable. Only the words ‘pity’ and ‘lament’ bode ill. What can they mean?” As his thoughts reached this point, he chided himself: “I am peeking at these in secret. If I go on standing here lost in foolish speculation and someone comes, I shall not be able to read any more.” So he continued reading, with no leisure to examine the pictures closely, and simply read onward from the beginning. Near the end he came upon several lines of verse, including the phrase “at our meeting, the great dream ends.” Suddenly enlightened, he said, “Yes, that is it! The hidden design proves unerring. This must surely be Elder Sister Yuanchun. If they are all as clear as this, I need only copy them out and ponder them carefully, and then I shall know without exception which of the girls will live long or die young, prosper or fall into hardship. When I return, of course I shall reveal nothing, but simply act as one who knows the future; that will spare me no end of idle worrying.” He looked about but found neither brush nor inkstone. Afraid that someone might come, he could only hurry on with his reading. He could just make out in one picture a figure flying a kite, but had no inclination to examine it. In great haste, he read through all twelve poems and songs. Some he understood at a glance, some yielded their meaning after a moment’s thought, while others remained rather obscure; he fixed them all firmly in his memory.

When he came to the line, “How enviable the actor’s good fortune; who knew the young lord was not destined for her?”—words he had not understood before—and saw that above them there still lingered the shadow of a flower-decked wedding feast, he burst into bitter tears.

p.src: Just as he was about to read on, he heard someone say, “You are lost in a daze again! Cousin Lin is asking for you.” The voice sounded like Yuanyang’s, but when he turned around, no one was there. While he was still startled and puzzled, Yuanyang suddenly appeared outside the door and beckoned to him. Delighted at the sight of her, Baoyu hurried out. But Yuanyang moved dimly ahead of him, and however he tried, he could not catch up. Baoyu called, “Dear sister, wait for me!” Yuanyang paid him no heed and simply continued onward. Helpless, Baoyu ran after her with all his strength, when suddenly another wondrous realm opened before him: tall towers and pavilions rose aloft, the corners of exquisite palace roofs gleamed, and many palace maidens could be glimpsed moving within. Absorbed in admiring the scenery, Baoyu forgot all about Yuanyang. Following the path, he entered a palace gate, within which grew strange blossoms and exotic plants, none of which he could identify. Only one blade of green grass, its leaf tips faintly tinged with red, was enclosed by a white-stone flower railing; he could not imagine what precious herb it might be to receive such honor. At the touch of a light breeze, the grass began to sway without cease. Though it was but a small, flowerless plant, its enchanting grace stirred his heart, delighted his spirit, and fairly ravished his soul. As Baoyu stood gazing at it in a trance, he heard someone beside him say, “What sort of fool are you, and where have you come from, that you dare spy upon an immortal herb?” Baoyu started at the words. Turning, he saw an immortal maiden and bowed to her. “I was looking for Sister Yuanyang and strayed by mistake into this immortal realm. Please forgive my presumption. May I ask, immortal sister, what place this is? And why did Sister Yuanyang come here and tell me that Cousin Lin was calling me? I beg you to enlighten me.” The maiden replied, “What do I know of your sisters and cousins? I am the guardian of this immortal herb, and mortals are forbidden to linger here.” Baoyu meant to leave, yet could not bear to do so, and pleaded, “Since you are the guardian of this immortal herb, immortal sister, you must surely be the Goddess of Flowers. But what special virtue does this plant possess?” The immortal maiden said, “If you wish to know about this herb, it is a long story. It originally grew on the bank of the River of Souls and was called the Crimson Pearl Plant. When it began to wither, it was fortunate enough to be watered daily with sweet dew by the Divine Luminescent Stone-in-Waiting, and so was preserved in life. Later it descended to the mortal world to undergo its destined trials and repaid the grace of that watering; now it has returned to the realm of truth. For that reason, the Fairy Disenchantment ordered me to guard it and keep bees from importuning it and butterflies from courting it.” Baoyu did not understand her words and remained convinced that he had encountered the Goddess of Flowers. Determined not to lose such an opportunity while face-to-face with her, he asked, “Then you, immortal sister, are the guardian of this herb. There must also be special guardians for the countless celebrated flowers. I would not dare trouble you by asking about them all, but which immortal has charge of the hibiscus?” The maiden replied, “That I do not know. Only my mistress would be able to tell you.”

You do not know that this Consort is my cousin Lin Daiyu.” “Nonsense!” said the immortal maiden. “This is the abode of divine maidens in the upper realm. p.src: Baoyu stood dumbfounded at her words, feeling himself filthy and unworthy. Just as he was about to withdraw, someone hurried up and said, “They are asking for the Divine Luminescent Stone-in-Waiting inside.” The first maiden said, “I was ordered to wait for him and have been here a long while, but no Divine Luminescent Stone-in-Waiting has appeared. Where am I supposed to go and invite him from?” The other laughed. “Was that not he who just withdrew?” The maid hurried out and called, “Divine Luminescent Stone-in-Waiting, please come back!” Baoyu assumed she was calling someone else, and, afraid of being pursued, fled away staggering. As he ran, a person carrying a sword suddenly barred his way and cried, “Where do you think you are going?” Baoyu was terrified and knew not what to do. Summoning his courage, he looked up and saw that it was none other than Third Sister You. At the sight of her, Baoyu recovered himself a little and pleaded, “Sister, why have you also come to persecute me?” She replied, “Not one of you brothers is a decent man. You ruin women’s reputations and destroy their marriages. Now that you have come here today, I shall not spare you!” Baoyu sensed danger in her words and was growing frantic when he heard someone behind him call, “Sister, stop him at once! Do not let him escape!” Third Sister You said, “I have waited here a long time by the Consort’s command. Now that I have found you today, I must sever all your mortal ties with a single stroke of my sword.” Baoyu grew more desperate still. Unable to understand what any of this meant, he could only turn and try to run. But the speaker behind him was none other than Qingwen. When Baoyu saw her, sorrow and joy mingled in his heart, and he said, “I lost my way while walking alone and encountered an enemy. I wanted to flee home, but not one of you was here to accompany me. Everything is all right now. Sister Qingwen, quickly take me home.” Qingwen replied, “You need not be suspicious, Stone-in-Waiting. I am not Qingwen. I have come expressly at the Consort’s command to invite you to meet her, and I mean you no harm.” Baoyu’s mind was full of doubt, and he had no choice but to ask, “You say the Consort has summoned me, sister—but who exactly is she?” Qingwen replied, “There is no need to ask now. You will know when we arrive.” Baoyu had no alternative but to follow her. Watching her closely from behind, he saw that every movement was exactly Qingwen’s; there could be no mistake about her face or voice. “Why, then, does she say she is not Qingwen? My mind is in a haze just now. Never mind her for the moment. Once I get there and meet the Consort, if anything is amiss, I can plead with her then. Women are compassionate at heart, after all, so she will surely forgive my presumption.” While he was thinking this, they soon arrived at a certain place. There stood exquisitely fashioned halls ablaze with brilliant colors; a cluster of emerald bamboo grew in the courtyard, and several ancient pines stood outside the doors.

p.src: Several maidens stood beneath the eaves of the corridor, all dressed in palace attire. When they saw Baoyu enter, they whispered, “Is this the Divine Luminescent Stone-in-Waiting?” The one who had led Baoyu there replied, “Yes, he is. Hurry inside and announce him.” One maid smiled and beckoned, and Baoyu followed her inside. After passing through several ranges of rooms, he came to a main chamber with its beaded curtain raised high. The maid said, “Stand here and await Her Ladyship’s command.” Hearing this, Baoyu did not dare utter a sound and could only wait outside. Before long the maid returned from within and said, “The Stone-in-Waiting is summoned to pay his respects.” Another maid rolled up the beaded curtain. Inside sat a woman wearing a flowered coronet and embroidered robes. Baoyu glanced up and, seeing that she looked like Daiyu, could not help exclaiming, “Sister, so this is where you are! How terribly I have missed you!” A maid outside the curtain rebuked him in a low voice: “What an ill-mannered Stone-in-Waiting! Leave at once.” Before she had finished speaking, another attendant lowered the beaded curtain. Baoyu longed to go in but dared not; he wished to leave but could not bear to. He wanted to ask what this meant, yet none of the maids was familiar to him, and since they were driving him away, he had no choice but to withdraw. Thinking to ask Qingwen, he looked all around, but she was nowhere to be seen. Deeply puzzled, he could only leave in dejection. With no one to guide him, he tried to retrace his steps, only to find that he could no longer locate the old path. While he stood there at a loss, he saw Xifeng beneath the eaves of a house, beckoning to him. Delighted at the sight, Baoyu said, “Thank goodness! So I have come back home after all. How could I have become so confused all of a sudden?” He hurried over and said, “Sister, are you here? Those people have tormented me beyond endurance. Sister Lin refuses to see me too, and I cannot imagine why.” As he spoke, he reached the place where Xifeng stood. Looking closely, he saw that it was not Xifeng at all, but Qin-shi, Jia Rong’s former wife. Baoyu stopped and was about to ask, “Where is Sister Xifeng?” But Qin-shi made no reply and simply went into the room. Still dazed, Baoyu dared not follow her inside. He stood there blankly and sighed, “What wrong have I done today that everyone ignores me?” Then he burst into bitter tears. Just then several Yellow-Turbaned Mighty Ones came charging at him with whips in hand, shouting, “What man dares intrude upon our blessed realm of celestial maidens? Get out at once!” Baoyu heard them and dared not speak. As he was about to search for a way out, he saw in the distance a group of women approaching, laughing and talking. Looking closer, Baoyu thought they resembled Yingchun and the others. Overjoyed, he called, “I am lost here! Come quickly and save me!” While he was still shouting, the Mighty Ones came rushing up behind him.

p.src: Just as Baoyu was in the greatest distress, the monk who had brought back the jade appeared, holding up a mirror whose light he cast upon them. “I have come expressly to save you,” he said, “by command of Her Highness Consort Yuan.” At once the demons vanished, and all around was once more a desolate wilderness. Baoyu seized the monk by the arm and said, “I remember it was you who led me here, and then you suddenly disappeared. I saw many of my loved ones, but none would pay me any heed; then suddenly they turned into demons. Was it a dream or was it real? I beg you, Master, to explain it clearly to me.” The monk asked, “While you were here, did you secretly look at anything?” Baoyu thought, “Since he can bring me to this blessed realm of celestial maidens, he must naturally be an immortal himself. How could I conceal anything from him? Besides, I want to have the matter explained.” So he replied, “I did happen to see quite a few registers.” “There you have it,” said the monk. “After seeing those registers, do you still not understand? All worldly bonds of passion are but those demonic snares. Only remember carefully all that you have experienced, and in time I shall explain it to you.” With these words he gave Baoyu a violent shove and said, “Go back!” Baoyu lost his footing and fell headlong, crying, “Ow!”

p.src: Lady Wang and the others were weeping when they heard that Baoyu had revived, and they hurriedly called out to him. When Baoyu opened his eyes, he found himself still lying on the kang and saw that Lady Wang, Baochai, and the others had eyes swollen red from weeping. Once he had collected himself and thought about it, he said inwardly, “Yes—I have returned from death.” He then stared blankly as he carefully recalled all that his spirit had experienced. Fortunately, he still remembered most of it, and he laughed aloud, saying, “Yes, that is it! That is it!” Lady Wang assumed that his old illness had returned and thought that now a physician could be summoned to treat him. She immediately ordered the maids and old serving women to hurry and tell Jia Zheng, “Baoyu has come round. His mind had merely been clouded before, but now he can speak again, so there is no need to prepare for his funeral.” On hearing this, Jia Zheng hurried in to see him. Finding that Baoyu had indeed revived, he said, “You ill-fated little fool! Whom are you trying to frighten to death?” As he spoke, tears began to flow before he was even aware of them. After heaving several more sighs, he went out again and ordered someone to fetch a physician to feel Baoyu’s pulse and prescribe medicine. Meanwhile, Sheyue had been contemplating suicide, but when she saw Baoyu come round, she too was relieved. Lady Wang then had a bowl of longan broth brought and made him drink a few mouthfuls, after which he gradually regained his composure. Lady Wang and the others were now reassured and said nothing to Sheyue. Lady Wang merely had the jade handed back to Baochai so that she could put it on him, and said, “Come to think of that monk, it is strange that no one knows where he found this jade. Why did he demand silver one moment and vanish the next? Could he have been an immortal?” Baochai said, “Judging from the strange manner in which that monk came and went, the jade was not something he had found. When it disappeared before, the monk must have been the one who took it away.” Lady Wang said, “But how could he have taken the jade when it was here in our house?” Baochai replied, “If he could bring it here, he could also take it away.” Xiren and Sheyue said, “The year the jade was lost, Master Lin interpreted a written character for us. Later, after Second Mistress married into the family, I told you that the character he had interpreted was something like shang, meaning ‘reward.’ Do you still remember, Second Mistress?” Baochai thought for a moment and said, “Yes, I remember. You said the interpretation meant it would be found in a pawnshop. Only now do I understand: the upper part of the character was shang, as in heshang, ‘monk.’ Does that not mean it was the monk who took it away?” Lady Wang said, “That monk was always a strange one. When Baoyu fell ill that year, the monk came and said that our family possessed a treasure that could cure him. He was referring to this very jade. Since he knew that, this jade must naturally have an extraordinary origin. Besides, your husband was born with it in his mouth. From ancient times to the present, have any of you ever heard of another such person? Only, I do not know what will ultimately become of this jade—or, for that matter, what will ultimately become of this son of ours.

p.src: His illness comes from this jade, his recovery comes from this jade, and even his life comes from this jade—” At this point she suddenly broke off, and tears once more began to flow. As Baoyu listened, he understood inwardly. His recent experience of death now seemed all the more clearly to have had a cause. He said nothing, however, and carefully recalled it all in his mind. Xichun then said, “When the jade was lost that year, we even asked Miaoyu to invoke the immortals. The message said, ‘Beneath Green Ridge Peak, leaning by an ancient pine,’ and there was also some line about ‘Enter my gate and meet me with a smile.’ Thinking back on it, the three words ‘enter my gate’ carry profound meaning. Of all spiritual paths, the Buddhist Dharma-gate is the broadest; I only fear that Second Brother may not be able to enter it.” On hearing this, Baoyu gave several more cold laughs. When Baochai heard this, she involuntarily knitted her brows and fell into a daze. Lady You said, “Whenever you speak, the subject somehow turns to Buddhism. Have you still not abandoned your desire to take religious vows?” Xichun smiled and said, “To tell you the truth, Sister-in-law, I gave up meat long ago.” Lady Wang said, “My dear child—Amitabha Buddha! You must not entertain such a thought.” Xichun heard her but said nothing. Baoyu thought of the verse about being “before the green lamp and ancient Buddha,” and could not help sighing several times. Suddenly he also remembered the verse about one sleeping mat and a single flower. He looked toward Xiren, and tears once more welled from his eyes. They all saw him laughing one moment and grieving the next, but none understood what it meant and merely assumed that it was his old illness. Little did they know that insight now came to Baoyu at every turn: he could clearly recall every line of verse in the register he had secretly read. He merely kept silent, for inwardly he had already formed a settled resolve. But we shall leave this aside for now.

p.src: Now, when everyone saw that Baoyu had returned to life after seeming dead, with his spirits clear and refreshed, and that after taking medicine for several days he improved day by day, they watched him gradually recover. When Jia Zheng saw that Baoyu was well again, he had no official duties while observing mourning. Reflecting that no one knew when Jia She might be pardoned, and still uneasy because the Old Lady's coffin had long remained at the temple, he wished to escort it south for burial and summoned Jia Lian to discuss the matter. Jia Lian said, “Your idea is perfectly right, sir. It would be best to accomplish this important undertaking now, while you are still in mourning. Once your mourning period ends and you return to office, I fear you may no longer be free to carry out your wish. But my father is away, and as his son and your nephew I dare not overstep my authority. Your plan is excellent, sir, but the undertaking will require several thousand taels of silver. There is no hope of the authorities recovering any more of the confiscated property.” Jia Zheng said, “My mind is made up. I summoned you only to discuss how it can be managed, since your father is away. You cannot leave home. There is no one else here now, and since several coffins must be taken back, how could I attend to them all alone? I thought I would take Rong with me. Besides, his wife's coffin is among them. There is also your Cousin Lin's coffin; the Old Lady left instructions that it should return together with hers. I think we shall have to borrow several thousand taels for this expense; that should be enough.” Jia Lian said, “Human feeling has grown far too cold these days. You are in mourning, sir, while my father is away; it will be impossible to obtain a loan at short notice. Our only course is to take out the deeds to some houses and land and mortgage them.” Jia Zheng said, “Our residence was built by the government. How could it be touched?” Jia Lian said, “The residence certainly cannot be touched. But we have several other properties that can be disposed of, and you may redeem them after you return to office. When my father returns, if he too should be restored to office, it will likewise be easy to redeem them. Only, at your age, sir, the thought of your enduring all the hardships of this journey leaves us nephews truly uneasy.” Jia Zheng said, “It is only right that I should attend to the Old Lady's affairs. You need only act prudently at home and keep a firm hand on everything.” Jia Lian said, “On that score you may set your mind entirely at ease, sir. Though I may be foolish, I would never dare conduct these affairs without the utmost care. Besides, you will naturally take many people south with you, leaving only a limited number here, so I should be able to meet these modest expenses. If you should run short on the road, you must pass through the place where Lai Shangrong is, and we can ask him to lend a hand.” Jia Zheng said, “This is our own elder's affair. Why should we ask help from others?” Jia Lian answered, “Yes,” then withdrew to make arrangements for the money.

p.src: Jia Zheng then informed Lady Wang and put her in charge of the household. He himself chose an auspicious day for the funeral procession and the long journey and prepared to depart. By then Baoyu had recovered, while Jia Huan and Jia Lan were applying themselves earnestly to their studies. Jia Zheng entrusted all three to Jia Lian's discipline, saying, “This year the provincial examinations will be held. Huan is in mourning and cannot enter the examination hall, but Lan, being a grandson, may sit the examination now that his term of mourning has ended. You must see to it that Baoyu goes to take it with his nephew. If even one of them becomes a provincial graduate, it will help redeem our family's disgrace.” Jia Lian and the others assented respectfully to his commands. Jia Zheng gave further instructions to those remaining at home and spoke to them at length. Only after taking leave of the ancestral shrine did he spend several days outside the city having sutras recited; then the funeral procession embarked, and he departed with Lin Zhixiao and the others. They did not trouble their relatives or friends; only the men and women of their own household accompanied them part of the way before returning.

p.src: Because Jia Zheng had ordered Baoyu to sit the examination, Lady Wang began pressing him frequently and inspecting his lessons. Needless to say, Baochai and Xiren also encouraged him constantly. Little did they know that although Baoyu's strength and spirits improved daily after his illness, his thoughts grew stranger than ever and underwent a complete transformation. Not only did he despise scholarly honors and official advancement, he had also grown much more indifferent to romantic attachments. The others scarcely noticed this, and Baoyu did not speak of it either. One day, Zijuan happened to return after seeing Lin Daiyu's coffin off. Sitting sorrowfully in her own room and weeping, she thought, “Baoyu is heartless. When he saw his Cousin Lin's coffin depart, he shed no tears of grief; and when he sees me crying like this, he does not come to comfort me but looks at me and laughs instead. What a faithless man he is! All those sweet words he used to say were merely meant to deceive us! Fortunately I came to my senses the night before last; otherwise I would almost have fallen into his trap again. Yet there is one thing I cannot understand: now he seems just as cold toward Xiren and the others. The Second Young Mistress was never fond of intimacy to begin with, but surely Sheyue and the others must resent him? I suppose most girls are foolishly devoted. After all the needless care they have lavished on him, let us see how it ends!” As she was thinking this, Wuer came to see her. Noticing Zijuan's tear-streaked face, she said, “Are you thinking of Miss Lin again, sister? Truly, hearing of a person is not the same as seeing him for oneself. I used to hear that Second Master Bao treated girls better than anyone, and my mother went to great lengths to get me admitted here. Who would have thought that after I came and devoted myself heart and soul to nursing him through several bouts of illness, now that he is well he cannot spare me a single kind word? These days he will not even look at me.” Zijuan found her words amusing and burst out laughing. She spat playfully, “Pah, you little minx! Just how do you want Baoyu to treat you? Have you no shame as a girl? Even among those who are properly recognized as members of his household, there is a whole crowd he pays no attention to. When would he have time for you?” Still laughing, she ran a finger across her own cheek in a gesture of mock shame and asked, “And just what are you to Baoyu, anyway?” Hearing this, Wuer realized she had spoken out of turn, and her face flushed scarlet. She was about to explain that she had not meant she wanted Baoyu to treat her in any particular way, but only that he had lately shown no kindness to his inferiors, when a clamor arose beyond the courtyard gate: “That monk has come again, demanding the ten thousand taels of silver! Her Ladyship is frantic and has sent for Second Master Lian to reason with him, but of all times, the Second Master is away from home. The monk is talking wildly outside, so Her Ladyship has asked the Second Young Mistress to come and discuss what to do.” How they managed to send the monk away will be told in the next chapter.

She was about to explain that she had not meant she wanted Baoyu to treat her in any particular way, but only that he had lately shown no kindness to his inferiors, when a clamor arose beyond the courtyard gate: “That monk has come again, demanding the ten thousand taels of silver!
Her Ladyship is frantic and has sent for Second Master Lian to reason with him, but of all times, the Second Master is away from home.
The monk is talking wildly outside, so Her Ladyship has asked the Second Young Mistress to come and discuss what to do.”
How they managed to send the monk away will be told in the next chapter.
